lines: +title: The package management API now has OpenAPI and SolrJ support. As part of this migration, the (experimental v2) API path moved from `/api/cluster/package` to `/api/cluster/packages`, and requests for a non-existent package or package version now return HTTP 404 instead of 400.

If an API returns specific, known additional data beyond these bases (e.g. timing information, computed ranges, a resource's status fields), extend the appropriate base with typed `@JsonProperty` fields rather than reaching for `FlexibleSolrJerseyResponse` - see `SplitShardResponse.timing`, `SplitCoreResponse.ranges`, or `CollectionStatusResponse` for examples.

Don't settle for a bare `SolrJerseyResponse` if the underlying operation actually produces more than a bare success/error - a v2 JSON caller has no other way to get that data, since (unlike v1) nothing else in the response pipeline will surface it (see the async caveat below for why this matters in practice).
+When an API exposes both a "list all" endpoint and a "get one by name" endpoint for the same kind of resource, give each its own response type rather than reusing the list's shape for a single item:
+* `List<Resource>Response` - the collection endpoint's response. Its data is a map or list keyed/indexed across every matching resource (e.g. `ListAliasesResponse.aliases: Map<String, String>`).

+* `Get<Resource>Response` (or `Get<Resource>ByNameResponse`) - the single-resource endpoint's response. Its data is a flat object describing just that one resource, with no collection wrapper (e.g. `GetAliasByNameResponse.collections`, `GetAliasByNameResponse.properties`).

+Don't have the single-resource endpoint return the list type filtered down to one entry (e.g. a `Map<String, ...>` with one key) - that forces callers to re-extract by name something they already specified in the request, and conveys no information once only one key is possible.
+See `ListAliasesResponse`/`GetAliasByNameResponse`, `ListClusterPropertiesResponse`/`GetClusterPropertyResponse`, and `ListPackagesResponse`/`GetPackageResponse` for examples of the pattern.
